summary: Karen Christina Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg and Geshe Ngawang Dhargyey, later teaching at the University of Virginia.

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from circa 1976 to 2009 and held multiple other academic posts.

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2013). She also studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago, and she taught Sally McAra.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London, where she was a senior teaching fellow, and served as a lecturer in Asian Religions and Ethics at the University of Roehampton in 2020.

Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy and studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held positions at the Free University of Berlin, the University of British Columbia, and the University of Hamburg before becoming a professor at the University of Vienna in 1999.

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1930 to 1934. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and served as Director of the Institute of Indology at the University of Halle.

Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at the universities of Jena and Helmstedt. He held long-term posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the École des Langues Orientales, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He served as Ordinarius at the University of Freiburg and later spent decades as Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at the University of Leipzig (1887–1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the universities of Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at the University of Heidelberg from circa 1836 to 1842.

Karl Eugen Neumann (1865–1915) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig and completed his doctoral studies under Richard Pischel between circa 1888 and 1891.
Karl Felix Halm (1809–1882) was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He held posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library from circa 1856 to 1882.
Karl Ferdinand Johansson (1860–1926) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University beginning in 1880 and later served as a professor there from circa 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz (1865–1939) worked in Japanology, linguistics, and religious studies, studying at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch and others. He taught at the University of Tokyo, the Hamburg Colonial Institute, and the University of Hamburg.

Karl Friedrich Geldner (1852–1929) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. After studying at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, he held positions at Tübingen, Halle, and Berlin, before serving as Sanskrit professor at Marburg from 1907 to 1921.
Karl G. Heider (born 1935) studied at Williams College from circa 1952 to 1953, Harvard College from circa 1953 to 1956, and Harvard University from circa 1956 to 1966.

Karl H. Potter (1927–2022) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of California and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Minnesota and the University of Washington and edited the Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies.
